title: Homotopy-category span isomorphisms lift to coherent equivalences
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor simplicial sets, mapping spaces and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a universe containing the data. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory, and let $K=\Delta^1\amalg_{\Delta^0}\Delta^1$ be the span simplicial set, with the source vertices identified. Write $h\mathcal C$ for the category with the vertices of $\mathcal C$ as objects and morphisms $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,y)$, with composition induced by two-simplices. Let $d,d':K\to\mathcal C$ be coherent spans with legs $u:d_a\to d_x$, $v:d_a\to d_y$ and $u':d'_a\to d'_x$, $v':d'_a\to d'_y$. Suppose isomorphisms $e_a:d_a\to d'_a$, $e_x:d_x\to d'_x$, $e_y:d_y\to d'_y$ in $h\mathcal C$ satisfy
$$e_x[u]=[u']e_a,\qquad e_y[v]=[v']e_a.$$
Then there exists an equivalence edge $\eta:d\to d'$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ whose three vertex components have classes $e_a,e_x,e_y$ in $h\mathcal C$. This only asserts existence of coherent span comparison, not a unique or contractible choice of such comparison.

source.place: Agent lemma isolating the coherent span comparison in the dual proof of Proposition 7.5.6, printed p. 373; restriction-isofibration and mapping-space conventions expanded using sections 3.5 and 4.2. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical lifting result.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], choose edges $\epsilon_b:d_b\to d'_b$ representing $e_b$ for $b=a,x,y$. Each $\epsilon_b$ is an equivalence, since its component class is invertible. Set $V=\{a,x,y\}\subset K$, the discrete simplicial subset of all vertices. The three edges define an edge $\epsilon:d|_V\to d'|_V$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(V,\mathcal C)$: degreewise, a map from $V\times\Delta^1$ is precisely three maps from $\Delta^1$. Choosing inverse edges and inverse-triangle witnesses for the three $\epsilon_b$ gives, component by component, an inverse and both triangle witnesses for $\epsilon$; hence $\epsilon$ is an equivalence edge. This uses only the actual equivalence witnesses, without identifying a homotopy-category isomorphism with an already coherent transformation on $K$.

source.place: Remark 4.6.8.14 and the homotopy-category equivalence criterion; agent assembly on the discrete vertex subset.

proof.text: The inclusion $V\hookrightarrow K$ is degreewise injective and both sets are small in the chosen universe. Apply the restriction clause of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to obtain an isofibration $r:\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(V,\mathcal C)$ between quasicategories. Its equivalence-edge lifting property applied at the object $d$ to $\epsilon:r(d)\to d'|_V$ supplies an equivalence edge $\eta_0:d\to d_0$ with $r(\eta_0)=\epsilon$ and $r(d_0)=d'|_V$. Thus $d_0$ has exactly the vertices $d'_a,d'_x,d'_y$. Write its legs as $u_0:d'_a\to d'_x$ and $v_0:d'_a\to d'_y$. The edges $\epsilon_b$ are the exact vertex restrictions of $\eta_0$.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.5.3, restriction isofibration, and the definition of its equivalence-edge lifting property.

proof.text: Restrict $\eta_0:K\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C$ to the $u$ leg. The square $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ has the two triangles with ordered vertices $((0,0),(1,0),(1,1))$ and $((0,0),(0,1),(1,1))$. Their common diagonal $w_x:d_a\to d'_x$ therefore satisfies $[w_x]=[\epsilon_x][u]=[u_0][\epsilon_a]$ by the two-simplex composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Comparing with the assumed equality gives $[u_0]e_a=[u']e_a$, so cancellation of the isomorphism $e_a$ gives $[u_0]=[u']$. Applying the same two-triangle calculation on the $v$ leg gives $[v_0]=[v']$.

source.place: Remark 4.6.8.10: two-simplices compute composition on components; explicit square triangulation and cancellation.

proof.text: Use the arrow mapping space $U_{\mathcal C}(s,t)=\{s\}\times_{\mathcal C}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)\times_{\mathcal C}\{t\}$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Its pinch inclusion is the identity on vertices (both vertex sets are edges $s\to t$) and induces a bijection on realized components. Step 3 consequently puts $u_0,u'$ in one component of the Kan complex $U_{\mathcal C}(d'_a,d'_x)$, and puts $v_0,v'$ in one component of $U_{\mathcal C}(d'_a,d'_y)$. By the component clause of [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre], each pair is joined by a finite zigzag of simplicial edges. Such a zigzag in a Kan complex gives a single edge with the required orientation: reverse an edge $f:p\to q$ by filling $\Lambda^2_0$ with edges $01=f$ and $02=\mathrm{id}_p$; the missing edge $12$ goes from $q$ to $p$. Compose successive oriented edges by filling $\Lambda^2_1$, and induct on the number of edges; for a zigzag of length zero use a degenerate edge. Obtain $h_u:\Delta^1\to U_{\mathcal C}(d'_a,d'_x)$ from $u_0$ to $u'$ and $h_v:\Delta^1\to U_{\mathcal C}(d'_a,d'_y)$ from $v_0$ to $v'$. The reversal and finite induction are direct uses of the Kan horn definition, not a further rectification theorem.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10 for pinch comparison; Hovey, Model Categories, Definition 3.4.1 and Lemmas 3.4.2-3.4.3 for components; explicit Kan two-horn argument.

proof.text: By the degreewise fixed-endpoint definition of $U$ in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], adjunction turns $h_u,h_v$ into maps $H_u,H_v:\Delta^1_{\mathrm{leg}}\times\Delta^1_{\mathrm{time}}\to\mathcal C$. They restrict at time $0$ to $u_0,v_0$, at time $1$ to $u',v'$, and on the leg-source edge to the same constant map at $d'_a$; their leg-target edges are constant at $d'_x,d'_y$. In each simplicial degree the product with $\Delta^1$ distributes over the pushout of the two leg sets along their source. These identifications respect all simplicial operators. Hence $H_u$ and $H_v$ glue to $H:K\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C$. The endpoints are exactly $d_0,d'$, so $H$ is an edge $\xi:d_0\to d'$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ whose three components are degenerate identity edges. No additional compatibility simplex is needed: $K$ is precisely the union of these two edges along the source vertex.

source.place: Arrow mapping-space definition; agent degreewise pushout and internal-Hom adjunction calculation.

proof.text: The functor simplicial set $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Fill its inner two-horn with edges $01=\eta_0$ and $12=\xi$, obtaining an edge $\eta:d\to d'$ on $02$. At each vertex $b$, evaluation of that two-simplex and [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] give $[\eta_b]=[\xi_b][(\eta_0)_b]=[\mathrm{id}_{d'_b}]e_b=e_b$. Each $\eta_b$ is therefore an equivalence by the same node's invertible-class criterion. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] with the small shape $K$ to conclude that $\eta$ is an equivalence edge. This proves existence with the prescribed three classes; no step imposes uniqueness on the path, lift, or horn-filler choices.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4 after inner two-horn composition; component computation as in Kerodon 01PF.
